content.text: You're a digital creator from a country that's been locked out of Stripe or PayPal. You've lost access to Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, or Paddle. Your customers can't even buy from you, and it's not just because of the 3% charge. You're in Zimbabwe, or perhaps Pakistan, or maybe it's the Philippines – in any case, you're about to lose everything if you can't figure out a way to get your digital store up and running. The solution isn't a workaround; it's a base-layer infrastructure that lets you own everything, from the code to the payment processing, without relying on anyone else. This guide will walk you through [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/setting-up-nowpayments-webhooks-cloudflare-workers-everything-you-2|setting]] up a Supabase order database for your digital store, and it starts with [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-payment-plain|COREMERCH guide to understanding]]-selling-design-assets-crypto-payments-plain-language-4|Understanding Selling]] why this infrastructure works when platforms fail.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The problem with relying on platforms like Stripe or PayPal is that they can shut you down at any moment. A change in regulations, a complaint from a competitor, or even a simple technical glitch can leave you without a way to process payments. And when that happens, your customers can't buy from you, no matter how much they need your product. But what if you could bypass the platforms altogether? What if you could set up your own infrastructure, one that lets you own the code, the payment processing, and the customer data? That's exactly what this guide is going to show you how to do, starting with the basics of why this infrastructure works when platforms fail.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can set up a Supabase order database for your digital store, you'll need to have a few things in place. First, you'll need to choose a hosting platform that can handle the load. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages are good options, as they offer free hosting and a range of customization options. You'll also need to set up a payment processing system that can handle cryptocurrency transactions. NOWPayments is a good option here, as it offers a range of features and zero fees for most transactions. And finally, you'll need to have a clear plan for how you're going to deliver your products to customers. This could be as simple as uploading files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, or as complex as setting up a custom delivery system using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once you've got your hosting and payment processing set up, it's time to start building your payment and delivery pipeline. This is where things can get a bit more complicated, but don't worry – we'll walk you through it step by step. First, you'll need to set up a Supabase instance to store your customer data and order information. This will involve creating a new database and setting up the necessary tables to store your data. Next, you'll need to integrate your payment processing system with your Supabase instance. This will involve setting up webhooks to trigger payment processing and delivery, and configuring your payment system to handle cryptocurrency transactions. Finally, you'll need to set up your delivery pipeline, which will involve uploading files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 or setting up a custom delivery system using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script.
The key to success with this infrastructure is to focus on scalability and customization options.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

With your payment and delivery pipeline set up, it's time to go live and start processing transactions. This is an exciting moment – you're finally going to see your infrastructure in action, and you'll be able to test everything to make sure it's working as it should. To do this, you'll need to deploy your infrastructure to a production environment and configure it to work with your chosen payment processing system and delivery pipeline. You'll also need to test everything to make sure it's working correctly, which may involve setting up fake customers and transactions to test the system. Once you're satisfied that everything is working as it should, you can start accepting real customer transactions and delivering your products to customers around the world.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is up and running, it's time to start thinking about scaling. This is where things can get a bit more complicated, as you'll need to consider factors like load balancing, caching, and content delivery networks to ensure that your infrastructure can handle the demands of a growing customer base. But don't worry – we'll walk you through it step by step. First, you'll need to set up a load balancing system to distribute traffic across multiple instances of your infrastructure. Next, you'll need to configure caching to speed up delivery of static assets and reduce the load on your infrastructure. Finally, you'll need to set up a content delivery network to ensure that your products are delivered quickly and efficiently to customers around the world.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The most important question you'll ask is 'How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?' The answer is simple: you use a base-layer infrastructure that lets you own the code, the payment processing, and the customer data. This guide will walk you through setting up a Supabase order database for your digital store, using a combination of GitHub Pages, NOWPayments, and Supabase to create a fully functional store that accepts cryptocurrency payments for free. With this infrastructure, you'll be able to bypass the platforms and build a store that's truly yours, without relying on anyone else.
Using a base-layer infrastructure lets you own the code, the payment processing, and the customer data, giving you complete control over your digital store.

Your Deployment Checklist

To set up a Supabase order database for your digital store, follow these steps: deploy your infrastructure to a production environment, configure your payment processing system to handle cryptocurrency transactions, set up your delivery pipeline to handle file uploads and downloads, deploy your infrastructure to a production environment, test everything to make sure it's working correctly, and configure your load balancing system to distribute traffic across multiple instances of your infrastructure. You'll also need to set up caching to speed up delivery of static assets and reduce the load on your infrastructure, and configure a content delivery network to ensure that your products are delivered quickly and efficiently to customers around the world.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 in COREMERCH?

Stack 01 is a basic deployment that includes GitHub Pages, NOWPayments, and Supabase – perfect for small digital stores that need to get started quickly. Stack 02 is a more advanced deployment that includes Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase – perfect for larger digital stores that need more scalability and customization options.
Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?
Yes – both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages offer free hosting and a range of customization options, making them perfect for digital product stores.
How long does it take to deploy Stack 01?
Deploying Stack 01 takes just 4-6 hours, following the Sovereign Blueprint.
What is the difference between NOWPayments and Stripe or PayPal?
NOWPayments is a cryptocurrency payment processing system that offers zero fees for most transactions, making it perfect for digital stores that need to accept cryptocurrency payments.
Can I use Cloudflare Workers to build a custom delivery system for my digital store?
Yes – Cloudflare Workers offers a range of features and customization options, making it perfect for building custom delivery systems for digital stores.
